channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Ontario seeks to add more primary care teams to attach 600,000 people
Fewer people running for trustee in some of Ontario's supervised school boards
item.description: The slate of municipal election candidates for school trustee in some boards under provincial supervision is set to be thinner than in the past, as would-be contenders face the prospect of running for a job they may not be able to do.

item.title: ‘If you have money, you can get out of jail’: Ontario’s new cash bail rules face constitutional challenge
item.description: Ontario’s new rules that require cash up front as part of being released on bail have been hit with a constitutional challenge on the same day they came into force.

item.title: Doug Ford says Ontario can’t let Donald Trump ‘control our data’
item.description: Premier Doug Ford says that failing to build data centres in Ontario risks 'Canadians’ data being sent to the U.S. and into the hands of (U.S.) President (Donald) Trump.'

item.title: ‘Stuff happens:’ Ford acknowledges PCs sent someone to surveil former Liberal leader on Jamaican vacation
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford is acknowledging that the Progressive Conservative party spent $3,000 on travelling to Jamaica to spy on Bonnie Crombie shortly after she became leader of the Liberal party in 2023 but he says he was not aware of the plan and doesn’t approve of it.

item.title: Ontario elementary teachers can buy classroom supplies from Staples using $750 spending cards
item.description: Ontario elementary teachers will be able to buy school supplies from Staples starting this fall.

item.title: New data centres will pay all energy costs, get no cash incentives under Ontario plan
item.description: Data centres in Ontario will need to cover all their energy costs and could pay more for electricity than other industrial users, the government said Thursday as it faces mounting pressure from local lawmakers to bring in guardrails around the facilities powering the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Doug Ford believes Toronto island airport will ultimately expand despite federal roadblock
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Thursday he believes his government will ultimately be successful in its push to expand Toronto’s island airport to allow jets to land, but he is not indicating how he’ll achieve that.

item.title: Ontario moves to make room for more casinos in Niagara Region
item.description: More casinos may be coming to the Niagara Region in the future, as the Ontario government has announced a deal to end existing exclusivity rights.

item.title: People in Canada illegally will no longer be eligible for social assistance in Ontario
item.description: Ontario is enacting new rules for social assistance payments so people without legal immigration status in Canada cannot receive the benefits.

item.title: Ontario government invests nearly $11M in health-care training from Skills Development Fund
item.description: The Ontario government announced Wednesday it will invest $10.9 million in training programs for nurses and other health-care professions.

item.title: Ontario cabinet minister calls for ‘all-out ban on AI deepfakes and impersonations’
item.description: An Ontario cabinet minister is calling on the federal government to enact “an all-out ban on AI deepfakes and impersonations.”

item.title: Ontario Line costs reach $34B, more than triple the original budget
item.description: The cost of building the Ontario Line has risen once again and Metrolinx CEO Michael Lindsay says that the total budget will remain “under pressure” amid “one of the worst supply chain shocks” in decades.

item.title: Candidates in Ontario Liberal leadership debate value of having a seat
item.description: Ontario Liberal leadership candidates are taking to the stage for the first debate in their race to lead the third-place party, with the early focus on whether it is important to have a seat.

item.title: Ontario launches reviews of large public agencies including Metrolinx, LCBO
item.description: The Ontario government is putting several large public agencies under the microscope, launching reviews that will look at efficiency and productivity.
